about: Third-party libraries self-hosted under assets/vendor/<name>/<version>/. Every file is byte-identical to its source URL, except a notice file marked written_by (a notice Orisod wrote about a library, never code); scripts/check_vendor.py (CI: check-vendor) checks each sha256 and size. See 'Self-hosted libraries' in CLAUDE.md for the update procedure.

libraries.name: spark-md5
libraries.license_note: Dual-licensed (WTFPL OR MIT); Orisod uses the MIT option, whose text is upstream's LICENSE2.

libraries.name: pdf-lib
libraries.license_note: The bundle also contains pako (MIT and Zlib), @pdf-lib/standard-fonts and @pdf-lib/upng (MIT), and tslib 1.x, whose Apache-2.0 notice is kept inside pdf-lib.min.js.

libraries.name: pdfjs
libraries.license_note: Mozilla's PDF.js (npm package pdfjs-dist); both files are identical to build/ in pdfjs-dist 3.11.174. Every getDocument() call must pass isEvalSupported: false (CVE-2024-4367; scripts/check_pdfjs.py). Pages set GlobalWorkerOptions.workerSrc to the vendored worker, so PDF.js starts it as a same-origin Worker.

libraries.name: jspdf-autotable
libraries.license_note: A jsPDF plugin, loaded right after jspdf.umd.min.js; 5.0.9 supports jsPDF 2, 3 and 4 (peer dependency jspdf ^2 || ^3 || ^4) and attaches doc.autoTable to window.jspdf.jsPDF on its own in the browser.

libraries.name: jszip
libraries.license_note: Dual-licensed (MIT or GPLv3); Orisod uses the MIT option. LICENSE is upstream's LICENSE.markdown unchanged, which holds both texts. jszip.min.js bundles pako 1.0.5, lie 3.3.0, immediate 3.0.6 and setimmediate 1.0.5 (versions from JSZip's v3.10.1 package-lock.json), all MIT; their license files are in notice_files.

libraries.name: docx
libraries.license_note: Not on cdnjs; this copy is the jsDelivr file, identical to dist/index.iife.js in the npm package. It exposes the global docx.

libraries.name: mammoth
libraries.license_note: Not on cdnjs; this copy is the jsDelivr file, identical to mammoth.browser.min.js in the npm package. It exposes the global mammoth.

libraries.name: xlsx
libraries.license_note: SheetJS Community Edition, from SheetJS's own CDN (current releases aren't on npm, cdnjs or jsDelivr); identical to dist/xlsx.full.min.js in the official xlsx-0.20.3.tgz. Its attribution header ("xlsx.js (C) 2013-present SheetJS -- http://sheetjs.com") is kept unchanged in the file; the package ships no NOTICE file. It exposes the global XLSX.

libraries.name: heic2any
libraries.license_note: heic2any is MIT. heic2any.min.js is unmodified (identical to dist/heic2any.min.js in the npm package; its sha512 equals cdnjs's SRI) and bundles libheif 1.10.0 and libde265 1.0.2 (both LGPL-3.0-or-later, compiled to JavaScript with Emscripten as an asm.js build, no WebAssembly) and gifshot (MIT, Yahoo; closest to 0.4.5, used only for GIF output). COPYING-libheif.txt and COPYING-libde265.txt are those projects' COPYING files at the bundled tags, with the full LGPL-3.0 and GPL-3.0 texts; LICENSE-gifshot.txt is gifshot's MIT license. NOTICE.txt (written by Orisod) names the bundled versions, how they were found, links to their source and says how to use your own build instead. The worker heic2any starts is a blob: URL built from code inside the file; it fetches nothing. The text files end in .txt so GitHub Pages serves them as text (an extensionless file is sent as application/octet-stream and downloads); their bytes are the upstream files'. source_archives are the libheif 1.10.0 and libde265 1.0.2 release archives from their GitHub releases, byte-identical (sha256 also in Homebrew's libheif 1.10.0 formula and meta-openembedded's libde265_1.0.2 recipe), hosted so the LGPL source is available from orisod.com; nothing loads them.

libraries.name: tesseract
libraries.license: Apache-2.0 AND MIT AND BSD-2-Clause AND BSD-3-Clause AND IJG AND libpng-2.0 AND libtiff AND Zlib AND ISC
libraries.license_note: tesseract.js 7.0.0 (Apache-2.0): tesseract.min.js (the cdnjs file, identical to the npm package's dist/ copy; sha512 equals cdnjs's SRI) and worker.min.js, each with the .LICENSE.txt published next to it (worker.min.js bundles buffer MIT, ieee754 BSD-3-Clause, regenerator-runtime MIT, zlib.js MIT). core/ holds the 3 LSTM-only builds of tesseract.js-core 7.0.0 (Apache-2.0) the worker picks from by browser support (relaxed SIMD, SIMD, neither); each .wasm.js embeds its WebAssembly. The core is built from Tesseract (Balearica's fork, Apache-2.0), Leptonica 1.83.0, libjpeg 9a (IJG), libpng 1.6.38, libtiff 4.3.0, giflib 5.1.4 (MIT), libwebp 1.2.2 (BSD-3-Clause), zlib 1.2.12 and openlibm 0.8.0, whose license files (at the commits tesseract.js-core v7.0.0 pins) are in core/. lang/ holds the 4.0.0_best_int eng and spa data of @tesseract.js-data/eng@1.0.0 and spa@1.0.0 (byte-identical to the unversioned jsDelivr URLs tesseract.js uses by default): integer LSTM models made by naptha/tessdata (Apache-2.0) from tesseract-ocr/tessdata_best (Apache-2.0); the npm packages declare MIT in package.json without a license text, so those package.json files are kept as the record. NOTICE (written by Orisod) lists every part, version, source and license file.

libraries.name: liberation-sans
libraries.license_note: Liberation Sans Regular and Bold, unmodified: byte-identical to the TTFs in the release tarball (release_archive), served as-is. The OFL's Reserved Font Name "Liberation" only restricts modified versions, so the files must never be subset, converted or re-saved. Loaded with fetch() only when a presentation or spreadsheet has characters outside Windows-1252 that the font covers (see the shared FONT_RANGES on the PowerPoint to PDF and Excel to PDF pages).

release_archive.checksum_from: Homebrew cask font-liberation (Casks/font/font-l/font-liberation.rb, version 2.1.5,7261482); the GitHub release publishes no checksum

libraries.name: libphonenumber-js
libraries.license_note: MIT. Its phone number metadata comes from Google's libphonenumber (Apache-2.0), whose license text the package ships as LICENSE.Apache (kept as a notice file). Orisod uses the max bundle, which tells mobile numbers from landlines, and the package's examples.mobile.json (one example mobile number per country) for the phone field's placeholder.

libraries.name: circle-flags
libraries.license_note: Only the flags of the 245 regions libphonenumber-js lists (FLAG_CODES on the page) are vendored. LICENSE is upstream's LICENSE.md.

libraries.name: inter
libraries.license_note: Inter 4.001 (Google Fonts build, git-66647c0bb), variable weight axis 100 to 900, roman only, as published in the npm package @fontsource-variable/inter 5.3.0 (the jsDelivr files, identical to the package's; tarball checked against npm's sha512 integrity). Only the latin and latin-ext subsets are vendored. The official rsms/inter release ships no subsets, so these are Fontsource's unmodified subset files; never subset, convert or re-save them. Loaded with @font-face from the shared tokens in assets/css/orisod.css (Orisod 2.0).

libraries.name: lucide
libraries.license_note: Lucide icons as published in the npm package lucide-static 1.72.0 (the jsDelivr files, identical to the package's; tarball checked against npm's sha512 integrity). Lucide is ISC; the icons derived from Feather (of these: moon, search, x) are also under Feather's MIT license, and the package's LICENSE, vendored unchanged, holds both notices. Only the icons the site uses are vendored. scripts/sync_nav.py reads them and writes them inline into the site menu of every page (Orisod 2.0), so no page loads these files.
